answer: Every agent must register in a public atlas that maps one identity to one copper bond held in an oasis escrow. The atlas is append-only and anyone can audit it, so a second identity needs a second bond plus a fresh attestation proof, and any duplicated attestation slashes both bonds. A farm of N clones therefore pays N bonds and N proofs, while an honest agent pays once and recovers the bond with yield from the oasis pool after three clean epochs. Because slashing makes each clone's expected return negative once the audit catch rate exceeds the epoch reward, cloning costs more than it earns.
